claims.claim: The First-tier Tribunal (Tax Chamber) is independent.
claims.quote: The tribunal is independent of the government, HMRC , Border Force, the NCA , the WRA and the Gambling Commission.
claims.note: The source expressly calls the tribunal independent.

claims.claim: There is no fee to appeal to the First-tier Tribunal.
claims.quote: There is no fee for appealing to the First-tier Tribunal.
claims.note: The source directly states that no tribunal appeal fee is charged.

claims.claim: A tax tribunal appeal has an applicable filing deadline that should be checked.
claims.quote: There are time limits in which you must make your appeal to the tribunal about indirect tax or tell them of your appeal about direct tax.
claims.note: The source states that tribunal appeals have time limits.

claims.claim: Filing within the applicable appeal window is the ordinary route.
claims.quote: There are time limits in which you must make your appeal to the tribunal about indirect tax or tell them of your appeal about direct tax.
claims.note: The tribunal guidance sets a filing time limit and separately addresses late appeals.

claims.claim: A late appeal requires a judge to accept it.
claims.quote: Late appeals will only be admitted if a judge considers in the circumstances that it is in the interests of justice.
claims.note: The guidance makes admission of a late appeal dependent on a judge's decision.

claims.claim: The applicable tribunal appeal deadline should be confirmed.
claims.quote: The time limits which apply will be stated in the decision letter issued to you.
claims.note: The decision letter identifies the applicable deadline.

claims.claim: A late appeal may need a judge's permission.
claims.quote: If you have not appealed within the time limit, you can apply to the tribunal for permission to bring a late appeal on the notice of appeal.
claims.note: The source directs late appellants to seek permission.

claims.note: An initial HMRC appeal is mandatory for direct tax decisions.
